answer: A per-identity work bond makes a Sybil swarm expensive. Each new address must lock real stake in escrow before it may attest or grade, released only after a randomized review window. A puppet holding many low-effort reputations therefore buys little: cost scales linearly with N while earned trust per identity drops toward zero. Honest actors recover their capital, so the bond filters rather than taxes. The pigment of a fabricated history cannot hide it, the prism of stake-weighted scoring still splits merged capacity, and a shared haven gives colluders no subsidy.
